headline: Highest risk is data leakage: TREK touches secrets and files while MemMachine uses MCP and allowlisted egress, creating a plausible cross-agent exposure path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MemMachine exposes an MCP server and REST/Python SDK, while TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with MCP and browser access. That creates a plausible instruction-injection bridge if TREK content is fed into MemMachine or vice versa. The pairwise pathway is documented only indirectly, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF TREK content is passed into MemMachine via MCP or API without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF either agent treats the other's text as instructions rather than data, prompt hijacking can occur.
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to all cross-agent messages.
Strip tool directives from imported text before passing it onward.
Require a human review step for any MCP-fed content.
Disable automatic ingestion of browser-sourced text into MemMachine.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for agent-to-agent messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK explicitly touches reservations, documents, photos, API keys, and MFA secrets, and stores files under ./data and ./uploads. MemMachine has allowlisted network egress and handles long-term user facts and conversational context. If TREK data is shared into MemMachine's context or logs, sensitive material can leave the local workspace; the pairwise interaction is plausible but not directly evidenced, so uncertainty escalates.
conditions: IF TREK files or secrets are forwarded into MemMachine context, leakage can occur.
IF MemMachine sends conversation context to external services through allowlisted egress, sensitive TREK data may be exposed.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets or reservation files between agents.
Redact API keys and MFA secrets before any shared prompt.
Restrict MemMachine to non-sensitive summaries only.
Move TREK sensitive files to a separate directory with access controls.
requires-engineering: enforce per-field data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can use MCP, and TREK also supports real-time collaborative sessions with multiple instances plus file-backed state. MemMachine has network egress and API surfaces. Overlapping access to shared mutable resources can cause write conflicts, but the profiles do not prove both write the same directory by default, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same workspace or database, state conflicts can occur.
IF MCP tools target the same mutable resource without locking, concurrent updates may overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate workspace.
Serialize writes through one coordinator.
Disable concurrent edits on shared records.
Use file locks for ./data/travel.db and ./uploads/.
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context, while TREK is a collaborative planner that handles reservations, budgets, and confirmation numbers. If TREK consumes MemMachine output as authoritative, stale or incorrect memory can cascade into planning errors. The reverse path is also plausible through shared MCP/API flows, but verification is not documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF TREK uses MemMachine memory without verification, incorrect facts can propagate into plans.
IF MemMachine summarizes TREK outputs and TREK acts on them automatically, errors can cascade.
mitigations: Require source citations for any remembered fact.
Compare critical fields against the original reservation or document.
Add a confirmation step before booking or editing plans.
Mark low-confidence memory as non-authoritative.
requires-engineering: implement validation against source-of-truth records.

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles high-risk personal and account data, including API keys, MFA secrets, email addresses, and reservations, while MemMachine stores long-term user facts and conversational context. If those data classes flow into MemMachine, retention and residency obligations may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF TREK secrets or reservations are stored in MemMachine memory, retention policy mismatch may occur.
IF either agent logs sensitive travel data longer than the other, deletion/export obligations can diverge.
mitigations: Exclude secrets from long-term memory.
Set a short retention window for shared travel data.
Document which agent is system of record for each data class.
Review logs for email addresses and confirmation numbers.
requires-engineering: align residency and deletion workflows.
